summary: Andrei Ivanovich Vostrikov (1904–1937) was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (Theodore Stcherbatsky).
Andrew B. Irvine works in philosophy and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Boston University and was an assistant professor of philosophy at Maryville College, attested in 2009.

Andrew Glass works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Bukkyo University (2003) and earned his MA (2000) and PhD (2006) from the University of Washington under Richard Salomon and Collett Cox.
Andrew J. Nicholson specializes in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under traditional teacher Shree Narayan Mishra and held a post at Stony Brook University.

Andrew Olendzki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Lancaster University. He served as executive director of the Insight Meditation Society, executive director and resident scholar at Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003–2014), and senior scholar at Mind & Life Institute (attested 2014).
Andrew P. Tuck is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who completed his studies at Princeton University.
Andrew Quintman works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jay L. Garfield and was an assistant professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Yale University, attested in 2015.
Andrew William Kennedy is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned his PhD at the University of Leeds under the supervision of Philip A. Mellor and Kim Knott, attested in 2006.

Andrey Klebanov specializes in Indology and linguistics. He completed his MA (2010) and PhD (2016) at the University of Hamburg under Harunaga Isaacson and Dominic Goodall, and served as a professor at Kyoto University, attested in 2019.

Andrey Terentyev is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Faculty of Philosophy at Saint Petersburg State University (~1969–1975) and held a post at the Museum of the History of Religion (~1978–1993).

Andrzej Gawroński (1885–1927) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Lviv University (~1902–1903) and Leipzig University (~1904–1907). He held posts at Jagiellonian University (~1912–1916) and Lviv University (~1916–1927).

András Róna-Tas specializes in linguistics, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (1950–1955), was a guest lecturer at the University of Vienna (1983–1984), and served as president of the International Association for Tibetan Studies (~1985–1989).

André Bareau (1921–1993) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Paris, École Pratique des Hautes Études, and Collège de France, later serving as Directeur d'Études at the EPHE (1956) and Directeur at the Collège de France (1971–1991).

André Couture is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Laval University (~1965–1971), EPHE (~1971–1977), and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1971–1977), and held a post at Laval University (~1979–2012).

André Padoux (1920–2017) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Paris. He directed the Institut Français Frankfurt (~1959–1964) and held CNRS posts from 1959, becoming Directeur de Recherche in 1982.

Andy Rotman specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock and Steven Collins, and held a post at Smith College (attested 2013–2017).

Angela Falco Howard works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She completed her doctorate at New York University's Institute of Fine Arts under Alexander Coburn Soper and served as a professor at Rutgers University, attested in 2005.
Angela Manderscheid is a scholar of Tibetology who held posts at the Free University of Berlin and the University of Oulu, where she was a researcher attested in 1998.

Angela Sumegi specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her PhD from the University of Ottawa and served as an assistant professor in the College of the Humanities at Carleton University, attested in 2008.

Angelo De Gubernatis (1840–1913) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Turin and Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber. He held professorships at the University of Florence (1863–1891) and Sapienza University of Rome (1890).
